KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry weather is expected during the majority of 
this week. However, periodic rain showers are expected in 
North-Central NY this Monday. Periodic rain showers are 
possible region-wide this Thursday into Thursday night.

Aloft, a ridge continues to build from the western Great Lakes
this morning and then settles over the Northeast United States
and vicinity this afternoon through tonight. At the surface, 
the ridge continues to affect our region as the embedded high 
pressure center wobbles generally SSW'ward from near Lake
Champlain to the Mid-Atlantic states. Dry weather persists in 
our CWA as stabilizing subsidence accompanies the ridge. Clear
sky gives way to increasing cloud cover, especially in the
mid/upper-levels, this afternoon through tonight as moist 
isentropic ascent precedes the axes of shortwave troughs 
embedded in primarily W'erly to NW'erly flow aloft. Lows should
reach the mid 20's to upper 30's around daybreak this morning 
as clear sky, weak or calm surface winds, and low humidity 
promote efficient radiational cooling. Warmer highs in the 
upper 50's to upper 60's are expected this late afternoon and 
should be followed by overnight lows mainly in the mid 30's to 
upper 40's around daybreak Monday as the WAA regime strengthens 
somewhat along the western flank of the low-level ridge. 

On Monday, cyclonic W'erly to WNW'erly flow aloft and embedded 
shortwave troughs are expected to impact our region. Variable
amounts of mainly mid/upper-level cloudiness are expected amidst
moist isentropic ascent ahead of the shortwave trough axes. At 
the surface, the aforementioned ridge will exit generally 
SE'ward and be followed by the SE'ward passage of a weak cold 
front during the late morning through early afternoon. A rather 
dry low-level atmospheric column should permit a dry cold front 
passage across most of our CWA. However, forcing for ascent
along the front should coincide with sufficient low-level 
moisture and permit the development of isolated to scattered 
and light rain showers across North-Central NY. Behind the 
front, another high pressure ridge builds from central Canada 
and vicinity. Afternoon highs should reach mainly the mid 50's 
to mid 60's.

During Monday night through Tuesday night, the surface ridge 
will continue to affect our region as the embedded high pressure
center moves from northern ON toward northern New England, 
while the ridge aloft builds from the Upper Midwest to the
eastern Great Lakes. Dry weather is expected as stabilizing 
subsidence accompanies the ridge. Low-level CAA behind Monday's
cold front passage will contribute to lows reaching mainly the 
lower 20's to mid 30's around daybreak Tuesday and highs 
reaching mainly the 40's to 50's late Tuesday afternoon. Weak or
calm surface winds, low humidity, and sufficient cloud breaks 
are expected to permit efficient radiational cooling very late 
Tuesday afternoon through daybreak Wednesday, when lows should 
reach mainly the lower 20's to mid 30's. On Wednesday through
Wednesday night, the ridge at the surface and aloft should exit
E'ward and allow a warm front starved of low-level moisture to 
sweep NE'ward through our region and usher-in a somewhat warmer 
air mass. Fair weather is expected to persist. Late afternoon 
highs should reach the lower 50's to lower 60's in North-Central
NY and the upper 50's to upper 60's elsewhere in our CWA.
Thereafter, overnight lows should reach the mid 30's to mid 40's
in North-Central NY and the lower 40's to lower 50's elsewhere
in our CWA around daybreak Thursday. 

Note: Clear sky or sufficient cloud breaks and weak or calm
surface winds should contribute to localized steam fog in the 
Black River Valley, Western Southern Tier river valleys, and the
lake valleys of the Finger Lakes Region during the predawn 
hours through about 10 AM EDT today through Wednesday, respectively.

W'erly to WNW'erly flow aloft and a series of attendant troughs
and ridges at the surface and aloft should affect our region
this Thursday through Saturday. Current odds favor primarily
dry weather as ridging should affect Western and Central NY
during the majority of the time period. However, a weak cold 
front should sweep E'ward through our region Thursday night. 
Periodic rain showers are possible along and ahead of this front
on Thursday into Thursday night due to moist isentropic ascent 
ahead of a shortwave trough axis aloft and low-level 
convergence/ascent along the front coinciding with sufficient 
low-level moisture. Unusually-mild weather for late October is 
expected courtesy of the largely zonal flow aloft.
